newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler-Benz to be hit by further sick pay protest.
newsitem.headline: Daimler-Benz to be hit by further sick pay protest.

text.p: Workers at German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG will launch a protest next week against plans to cut workers' sick pay, the company's works council said Friday.
"The work force will manifest its protest in a number of ways" on Tuesday, Karl Feuerstein, head of the works council, said in Stuttgart. Daimler employs 220,000 people in Germany.

The new threat of industrial action follows unrest at Daimler-Benz's Mercedes-Benz plant in Bremen on Thursday, where workers angry at the cut in sick pay benefits disrupted the production of around 1,000 cars, according to representatives there.
A wave of German companies has followed Daimler-Benz's lead in announcing cuts in sick pay under a law taking effect Oct. 1 that cuts sick pay to 80 percent of normal wages.

Under the old law, sick pay was paid at 100 percent of normal salary, totalling some 60 billion marks ($40 million) in 1995. German corporate leaders have said the policy was abused on top of liberal holiday allowances.

Unions and some top politicians say German companies have no right to make the sick pay cutback so quickly, arguing that the bill, passed by Bonn earlier this month, was not meant to apply to existing contracts, but only future ones.
Udo Richter, head of the Bremen works council, warned that in light of the current mood of the employees, he expected that workers would not show up for scheduled extra shifts on Saturday.
The Bremen works, which produces Mercedes C-class and SLK models, employs about 13,500 workers. Cancelling of the Saturday shift would disrupt the production of around 300 cars.
The works council said so far only production of the C-class had been hurt and that the hot-selling SLK had not felt much impact from the protests.
